concepts.description: The acceptance test written alongside a feature, not the requirement or story that prompted it, is the artifact a future maintainer should trust as the record of intended behavior.
concepts.title: Acceptance Tests as Durable Behavior Record

concepts.description: Whoever built a system is a poor judge of how confusing it will be to someone inheriting it, because familiarity has already erased the difficulty for them.
concepts.title: The Author's Blind Spot for Complexity

concepts.description: Encoding which changes are safe, discouraged, or prohibited as automated, conspicuous checks rather than relying on a maintainer having read and remembered a prose warning.
concepts.title: Automated Guardrails for Safe Changes

concepts.description: Designing documentation for temporary system states (like migrations or parallel run phases) to decay and be removed once the transition is complete.
concepts.title: Biodegradable Documentation

concepts.description: A single named file collecting explanations for concerns that span multiple modules with no natural single home, referenced by short pointer comments at every touch point.
concepts.title: Central File for Cross-Module Design Notes

concepts.description: A system or initiative that survives only because one enthusiastic individual personally defends it decays once that person leaves, even if nothing about the system itself changed.
concepts.title: Champion-Dependent Projects

concepts.description: Classifying a prospective change by how many elements it touches predicts how risky and how staged a maintainer's rollout needs to be.
concepts.title: Change Scope Classification (Local, Nonlocal, Architectural)

concepts.description: Writing a test that pins down what a piece of undocumented legacy code currently does, before changing it, so a change can be verified safe without first understanding why the code behaves that way.
concepts.title: Characterization Tests for Undocumented Behavior

concepts.description: Verifying that the physical or logistical resources a checklist step depends on are reliably available before attributing compliance failures to operator discipline.
concepts.title: Checklist Compliance Precondition Audit

concepts.description: Running an operational checklist as a spoken, team-led ritual rather than a silent solo paperwork exercise, including who has authority to invoke it.
concepts.title: Checklist Execution as Team Communication

concepts.description: The two complementary purposes a checklist item can serve — forcing a predictable step to happen, or forcing team members to exchange information — and why complex operations need both.
concepts.title: Checklist Forcing Function Types

concepts.description: Criteria for deciding which steps earn a place on a short operational checklist when many candidate items compete for limited space.
concepts.title: Checklist Item Selection Trade-offs

concepts.description: A five-step discipline for extracting an expert operator's perceptual and judgment skills — not just their procedures — before that expertise leaves with them.
concepts.title: Cognitive Task Analysis for Capturing Tacit Expertise

concepts.description: A handover or instruction that states only the steps to follow leaves the recipient unable to adapt correctly when reality deviates from the plan; stating the underlying purpose is what lets them improvise instead of guessing.
concepts.title: Communicating Intent for Improvisation

concepts.description: Satisfying the actual knowledge, traceability, and control needs behind a compliance framework's documentation requirement instead of producing documents that only exist to check the audit box.
concepts.title: Compliance in Spirit vs. Ceremonial Documentation

concepts.description: A structured retrospective interview technique that surfaces an expert's tacit judgment by walking back through a specific difficult incident and probing each decision point, rather than asking generic questions about what they know.
concepts.title: Critical-Decision-Method Interview for Eliciting Expertise

concepts.description: A schedule that specifies who must consult whom, and by when, to resolve issues at the boundaries between specialties, as a companion to a process checklist.
concepts.title: Cross-Specialist Communication Schedule

concepts.description: Pushing operational decision-making to frontline operators under complex or nonroutine conditions, while centralizing communication and logistics support rather than the decisions themselves.
concepts.title: Decentralized Authority for Complex Operations

concepts.description: Enumerating every combination of diagnostic conditions as an explicit table or tree forces complete coverage that nested prose conditionals silently omit.
concepts.title: Decision Tables for Branching Diagnostics

concepts.description: Repeatedly stretching a maintenance or inspection interval in small, individually-justified steps can silently erode a system's real safety margin, because each step looks locally reasonable and "nothing broke" is mistaken for proof the new interval is safe.
concepts.title: Decremental Drift in Maintenance Intervals

concepts.description: Assigning a specific team or role ownership of failure investigation and checklist/runbook revision, rather than leaving operational documentation to accumulate ad hoc.
concepts.title: Dedicated Function for Operational Learning

concepts.description: Managing the deprecation of documentation as a structured migration process to guide users safely to supported alternatives.
concepts.title: Documentation Deprecation as User Migration

concepts.description: Connecting documentation updates to software development and release pipelines to prevent stale or harmful content.
concepts.title: Documentation Maintenance Workflows

concepts.description: Distinguishing failures caused by not applying known knowledge consistently from failures caused by not having the knowledge at all, to scope what operational documentation can actually fix.
concepts.title: Documentation Targets Ineptitude, Not Ignorance

concepts.description: Preserving distinct documentation for different supported versions of a system to avoid user confusion.
concepts.title: Documentation Version Boundaries

concepts.description: The operational rule requiring all emergency patches and hotfixes to pass through the standard automated delivery pipeline to prevent regressions.
concepts.title: Emergency Fix Pipeline Rule

concepts.description: Using annotations, sidecar files, or metadata registries to document a system without modifying it, for cases where touching the code directly is too risky.
concepts.title: External Annotations for Fragile Legacy Systems

concepts.description: A visual flowchart of a multi-step operational procedure is often less ambiguous and easier to follow correctly than the equivalent text-based, step-numbered writeup.
concepts.title: Flowcharts for Procedural Documentation

concepts.description: Two written onboarding formats — an orientation map and a narrated code route — that stay useful only if kept linked to and refreshed with the actual source.
concepts.title: Guided Tours and Sightseeing Maps

concepts.description: Approaching handover documentation as selecting and arranging existing knowledge for people who weren't present, adding only what's genuinely missing, rather than authoring a new account from scratch.
concepts.title: Handover Documentation as Curation

concepts.description: With enough users of an interface, every observable behavior becomes something somebody depends on, whether or not it was ever documented or promised.
concepts.title: Hyrum's Law

concepts.description: Four properties — reproducibility, idempotency, composability, and evolvability — that make infrastructure code safe for an unfamiliar operator to change without first understanding everything about it.
concepts.title: Infrastructure-as-Code Properties for Safe Change

concepts.description: Writing operational documentation only when a real knowledge gap is demonstrated, using disposable notes and a backlog rather than trying to document everything upfront.
concepts.title: Just-in-Time Documentation Triggers

concepts.description: Comparing self-managed launch readiness reviews with the more stringent handoff readiness reviews used when transferring service management to operations.
concepts.title: Launch vs. Handoff Readiness Reviews

concepts.description: Covering a complex, high-volume operation with several complementary, purpose-specific checklists rather than one comprehensive checklist.
concepts.title: Layered Checklist System Design

concepts.description: Why simple, standardized, easily-transmitted behavioral triggers change operator behavior at scale where comprehensive expert documentation does not.
concepts.title: Leverage Interventions vs. Comprehensive Guidelines

concepts.description: Structured collaborative sessions that transfer tacit system knowledge during a handover more reliably than written documentation alone.
concepts.title: Live Knowledge Transfer Techniques

concepts.description: Bringing a legacy, poorly-documented system up to a new documentation standard incrementally at the edges of active work, rather than attempting to document the whole system at once.
concepts.title: Marginal Documentation Migration

concepts.description: Designing a structured, cumulative learning path to build independent operating competence in new on-call engineers.
concepts.title: On-Call Onboarding and Training

concepts.description: A recurring, structured briefing between outgoing and incoming on-call engineers that transfers in-progress context, not just the pager.
concepts.title: On-Call Shift Handover Briefing

concepts.description: Treating how easy a system is for an operator to run day-to-day as a deliberate design goal alongside correctness and performance, not an afterthought left to documentation.
concepts.title: Operability as a Design Property

concepts.description: Key components that must be documented and agreed upon by development and operations before releasing or handing over a system.
concepts.title: Operational Release Readiness Plan

concepts.description: Safely transferring operational ownership of systems between product and operations teams to avoid communication gaps and operational degradation.
concepts.title: Operational Responsibility Transition

concepts.description: A structured, phased approach to recover a system from operational overload by embedding operations experts to clean up friction before handing support back.
concepts.title: Operational Stabilization Framework

concepts.description: Requiring development teams to support a new service in production for a set period before handoff to ensure operational stability.
concepts.title: Operational Warranty Period

concepts.description: Making a server disposable and automatically rebuildable from scratch so a new operator never needs to know its manual configuration history.
concepts.title: Phoenix Server Pattern

concepts.description: Documentation survives and gets updated only if it sits where the person changing the system will actually be looking, which is rarely the commit log and rarely a header file separated from the implementation.
concepts.title: Place Documentation Where Maintainers Will Look

concepts.description: Balancing the trade-off between flexible, judgment-based playbooks and rigid, step-by-step procedures to manage documentation decay.
concepts.title: Playbook Maintenance Tension

concepts.description: An operational playbook must layer business judgment (when, who to notify, what to verify) on top of the technical how-to, and should be authored jointly by developers and operators.
concepts.title: Playbook Required Content Elements

concepts.description: Building and refining checklist items by systematically cataloguing past mistakes across every stage of a process, rather than deriving items from theory alone.
concepts.title: Postmortem-Derived Checklist Items

concepts.description: Classifying an operational task as simple, complicated, or complex to decide what kind of documentation and coordination approach it needs.
concepts.title: Problem Complexity Taxonomy

concepts.description: A structured framework to audit and improve service architecture and operational readiness before launching or handing over a service.
concepts.title: Production Readiness Review

concepts.description: Treating the amount of explanatory prose a system requires as something to minimize by design, not just something to write more of.
concepts.title: Reducing Documentation Need Through System Design

concepts.description: A recovery or failover procedure that is only ever invoked during a real emergency loses reliability over time, so it must be exercised on a schedule via deliberately induced failures.
concepts.title: Rehearsing Rare Procedures with Deliberate Drills

concepts.description: Locating and publishing knowledge that already exists in an authoritative form — standard vocabulary, public references, or tool histories — instead of transcribing it into a new, separately-maintained document.
concepts.title: Reuse Existing Authoritative Sources Before Writing New Documentation

concepts.description: Designing operational checklists and runbooks that can be executed accurately under stress without causing cognitive overload.
concepts.title: Runbook and Checklist Design

concepts.description: Using declarative, inspectable automation (configuration, deployment, dependency definitions) as the source of truth so the system documents its own current state instead of relying on separately-maintained prose.
concepts.title: Self-Documenting Declarative Systems

concepts.description: Decoupling slow-changing domain orientation from fast-decaying implementation details to ensure documentation remains maintainable.
concepts.title: Separating Stable and Volatile Knowledge

concepts.description: Retiring a service safely requires an ordered, cumulative checklist covering user removal, resource deallocation, and resource disposal, because skipped or misordered steps leave orphaned resources or break still-dependent systems.
concepts.title: Service Decommissioning Checklist

concepts.description: Handing operational support responsibility back to the development team when a production service becomes excessively fragile or creates too much operational toil.
concepts.title: Service Handback Mechanism

concepts.description: A system that has been hand-configured through undocumented, ad-hoc changes to the point that it cannot be reliably recreated from any written record.
concepts.title: Snowflake Servers

concepts.description: A newcomer needs at least three different diagram types, not one, because each answers a different orientation question a single "architecture diagram" can't cover on its own.
concepts.title: Structural Views for Onboarding

concepts.description: A new operator must know what a system's normal behavior looks like before they can recognize what's abnormal, and must calibrate how rare a cause is likely to be given the system's scale and age.
concepts.title: System Baseline for Troubleshooting

concepts.description: AI coding and operations agents accelerate the loss of institutional knowledge that used to accumulate as a side effect of engineers personally authoring, debugging, and reviewing their own systems.
concepts.title: Tacit Knowledge Erosion Under AI-Assisted Work

concepts.description: Different recipients of a handover need different subsets of the same material, so a single all-purpose document under-serves everyone rather than serving any of them well.
concepts.title: Tailoring Documentation to Recipient Role

concepts.description: A live exercise where one person must explain a system's architecture starting from the barest essential summary and adding detail only as needed, forcing the team to separate what's essential from what's merely expedient.
concepts.title: Telling the Story of the System

concepts.description: Why a locally-reasonable substitution or deviation from an approved design must be routed back through the original design authority before being applied.
concepts.title: Unauthorized Substitution Change Control

concepts.description: A control, gate, or approval step that outlives the reason for its existence because that reason was never written down, turning into pure friction no one can safely remove.
concepts.title: Undocumented Rationale and Zombie Process

concepts.description: A written agreement documenting what an external data or system dependency actually provides, how, and who to contact, so a new maintainer isn't left reverse-engineering someone else's system under pressure.
concepts.title: Upstream Dependency Contract
